**Created file:** `E:/Hackathon/buddy-agent/app/item_update.py` ### 📌 Summary of the added endpoint & schemas | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Router** | `APIRouter` instance exported as `router` for easy inclusion in the main FastAPI app. | | **Request schema** | `ItemUpdate` – Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` with **optional** fields: `name`, `description`, `price`. | | **Response schema** | `ItemResponse` – Pydantic `BaseModel` containing `id`, `name`, `description`, `price`, and `updated_at` (`datetime`). | | **Endpoint** | `PUT /items/{item_id}` – accepts `item_id` as an integer path parameter and a JSON body matching `ItemUpdate`. Returns `ItemResponse` (status 200) with mock data:
• Echoes back the supplied `item_id`.
• Uses provided fields or fallback placeholder values (`f"Item {item_id}"`, `"Default description"`, `0.0`).
• `updated_at` set to current UTC time. | | **Imports** | `fastapi.APIRouter`, `pydantic.BaseModel`, `typing.Optional`, `datetime.datetime`. | | **Usage** | In the main FastAPI app you can simply do:
`from app.item_update import router as item_update_router`
`app.include_router(item_update_router)` | The file is ready to be imported and used by the main FastAPI application without any database or ORM dependencies.
